about: MUTATING — starts a STOPPED Forgejo on the forge again (infra/forge/move-forgejo-data.sh --restart; backlog 85d29e33, the re-review of move-forgejo-data). A failed proof of move-forgejo-data or roll-back-forgejo-data-move stops Forgejo, because a Forgejo whose data a run cannot vouch for must not take pushes; until this verb nothing but a root shell could start it again. In design 17835005's shape and authorised per run by David's passkey: it declares requires_approval with plan-a-forgejo-restart as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders and changes nothing unless the bytes hash alike. It takes no path. The plan names what Forgejo will serve: /opt/forgejo/data as the move's bind of <boss-data mount>/forgejo-data (by UUID), or as a directory holding data on the root filesystem; every other state — Forgejo running, the path absent, the empty mountpoint without its bind, a mount that is not the move's, no repository under it — is refused, exit 78, nothing changed. Its one act is docker compose start forgejo, which must be a real start (StartedAt moves), then it waits for /api/healthz to pass; main inside the container and the container's /data by device and inode are printed, and a leg that cannot be read or differs is a FINDING, never a stop — this verb never stops Forgejo. It neither places nor releases the converge hold. A start that fails or is not real, or a healthz that never passes, is exit 1 with what stands printed.
